## [M2 — the session runs: lege-comp on Smithay, graphical greeter, Home Surface and dock](ROADMAP.md#m2--the-session-runs-lege-comp-on-smithay-graphical-greeter-home-surface-and-dock) `@legeos.milestone.m2-session-runs/1`

### Home Field — the desktop surface: tiles, parked sessions, go-home, stable grid, projects, trays, previews

`proposed` · `@legeos.work.home-field/1` · part of `@legeos.milestone.m2-session-runs/1`

Replace the drawer-list Home Surface with the Home Field: a bounded field of rectangular tiles (projects, apps / parked sessions, file trays, widgets, system) on the shell's Layer::HomeSurface backdrop. Windows collapse into tiles instead of minimising and expand back out; Super+D / Ctrl+Alt+H / a dock Home button reveal the field temporarily without changing any window's state; dragging a tile onto a target performs a typed, previewed, undoable operation; layout is a stable local grid that never reflows globally, persisted per output by sessiond (org.legeos.HomeField1). Phases: 1 compositor truths (shelved windows actually hidden and not hit-tested, maximize, reveal-home command + keybindings + protocol v2 with identifier/geometry), 2 the pure crates/lege-field model (document, ops with inverses, local reflow, representation ladder, drag/throw state machine), 3 FieldScreen in lege-shell with --print field and full keyboard reach — the named Windows-8 fallback checkpoint — then 4 HomeField1 persistence, 5 projects/trays/zoom, 6 previews over ext-image-copy-capture, 7 lege-treemap (lifted from Silvaview-rs) and budgeted widgets, 8 the throw spike with a keep/delete rule. Plan of record: ~/.claude/plans/for-this-project-i-crispy-shannon.md (author's machine).

## Unparented

### Declare every user-facing action once, and generate the menu, the cheat sheet and the CLI verb from it

`proposed` · `@legeos.work.action-manifest-one-declaration-three-surfaces/1`

LegeOS already commits to every capability being reachable from the CLI, the portal, the shell and Settings (M1 evidence m1-clients-reachable; docs/architecture/accessibility.md: "everything the shell shows is available through lege too"). Today that is a discipline maintained by hand across four implementations, and nothing prevents them drifting. Omarchy demonstrates the mechanism that makes it structural: one declaration — `o.bind(chord, human_label, action)` — is simultaneously the keybinding, the row in a mouse-navigable menu tree, and the entry in a cheat sheet generated from the same table, so the documentation cannot fall out of date with the behaviour because it is not a separate artefact. Adopt the pattern: an action manifest (id, human label, optional chord, CLI verb, availability predicate) living in a service crate rather than the shell, with the shell's menu, the discoverability surface and `lege`'s subcommand table all rendered from it. The manifest belonging to a service rather than the shell is what keeps it consistent with services-not-indicators: the shell renders the manifest, it does not own it.
